This research aims to create a procedure and design framework for implementing ChatGPT as a tool with IT Engineering to support disabled students in extracurricular activities. The analysis of student feedback will also be used to revise the procedure and the design framework further. With it, the disabled student will be able to carry out their task closely with the normal students. The procedure and framework from the research result could also be used as a reference for other campuses to help their disabled student in the extracurricular program.

articleTitle: Understanding Digital Marketing Adopted by Small Travel Agencies Using Diffusion of Innovation Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The importance of adaptation in facing changes in the business world is a skill needed by every business actor. This also applies to businesses running in the tourism sector. Digital marketing is a concept that can be implemented to increase business expansion. Digital marketing can provide business people with wider space to be able to introduce their business to a wider target audience. However, not all companies are able and willing to adopt digital marketing values. This study aims to re-examine the Diffusion of Innovation theory within small travel agencies in East Java, Indonesia. A total of 150 companies were analyzed to assess their adaptation to changes in digital marketing strategies. The analysis was conducted using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The findings indicate that ease of use is the primary factor influencing these companies to shift their strategies towards digitalization.

articleTitle: Blockchain in Digital Document: A Review of Trends and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This literature review paper provides a comprehensive examination of recent advancements in blockchain technology with a focus on its application in digital security, document management, verification, and smart document integration. The review is organized into four main clusters: Security and Digital Verification, Document Management and Storage, Document Verification and Integrity, and Technology Integration with Smart Documents. In the Security and Digital Verification cluster, the paper explores the role of cryptography and digital signatures, particularly within blockchain frameworks, to enhance transaction security. The Document Management and Storage cluster search into the use of blockchain for secure data management in sectors like education and law. The Document Verification and Integrity cluster discusses decentralized approaches to verifying the authenticity of digital and hardcopy documents. Finally, the Technology Integration and Smart Documents cluster highlights innovations in combining distributed databases with technologies like QR codes to create and manage intelligent documents. This review identifies key trends, challenges, and potential areas for future research in the implementation of blockchain technology across various domains.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Medical Ethics Violations on the Effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence in Telemedicine
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: In recent years, telemedicine has become very important in the world of healthcare. In particular, the use of telemedicine has increased during the Covid-19 global pandemic. Through telemedicine, patients get remote services through information technology. Along with the development of AI today, AI has also been implemented in telemedicine and has provided many benefits to the health industry. However, there have been cases in the implementation of AI that have caused violations of medical ethics that have raised concerns, including AI issuing prescriptions without supervision, which can result in organ damage and even death. This study evaluates the impact of medical ethics violations on the effectiveness of AI in telemedicine. Systematic Literature Review (SLR) is used as the research method. The keywords used in this study are “telemedicine”, “artificial intelligence”, “medical ethics” from Scopus and Pubmed databases. A variety of studies were included in the review, including clinical trials, case studies, and theoretical frameworks. The review identified several trends, including the growing reliance on AI for diagnosis and treatment recommendations. In addition, recurring concerns were identified regarding the potential for bias and the security of the data. The findings indicate that violations of medical ethics can significantly impede the efficacy of AI in telemedicine, particularly with regard to ethical principles such as beneficence, nonmaleficence, autonomy, and justice. Such violations include infringements upon the right of patients to refuse AI-driven treatment, the transmission of unsecured data, the occurrence of data breaches, erroneous diagnoses, and the presence of bias in AI-generated recommendations. These issues have a deleterious impact upon patient safety and trust, result in a reduction of the accuracy of AI-facilitated diagnoses, and perpetuate health inequalities, ultimately eroding public trust and acceptance of AI in healthcare.

articleTitle: Potential Drop Out Students: Utilizing C4.5 Algorithm and Naive Bayes Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This research aims to determine the performance value of the implementation of the C4.5 and Naive Bayes Classification (NBC) algorithms, as well as the factors that influence students' failure to complete their studies on time. This study aims to predict the percentage of students who graduate and those who may drop out and compare the performance of two proposed models. This research uses training data for students in the Department of Information Systems class of 2010–2015 and test data for the class of 2018. The data mining process uses the sample, explore, modify, model, and assess (SEMMA) framework to process data and conduct comprehensive modeling. The results show that the C4.5 algorithm has an accuracy of 94.44%, while NBC has 93%. As a result, passing all courses, completing internship reports, and working on the final project report contribute to students' failure to graduate on time. This research contributes to the model of the two algorithms, their performance in predicting students who have the potential to drop out, as well as factors that influence the failure of students to graduate on time.

articleTitle: The Study Examines the Direct and Indirect Effects of Religiosity on the Productivity of Software Developers
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The expansion of the internet has resulted in its utilization in several manners. All of this needs some kind of program or computer system, which means someone who knows how to code is needed. This person is called a software developer. The number of software developers and the growth in Internet users exhibit a non-linear correlation. A number of similar studies say that non-technical factors have a bigger effect on how well and how quickly a software worker works than their technical skills. This study uses religion as an internal factor that affects how software developers act at work. It does this by using the results of an interview with a software developer who said that doing religious activities made them feel more focused and calmer when they were working. SEM-PLS was used to handle questionnaire data by researchers. The study tool used did a great job of representing the suggested mode. However, it was discovered that religiosity does not have a positive effect on work behaviour but does have a positive effect directly to productivity. On the other hand, work behaviour does have a positive effect on software developer productivity.

articleTitle: Aligning Healthcare Strategies Through Digital Information and Technology: Challenges and Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This study explores the challenges and solutions in implementing information technology in primary healthcare, focusing on Electronic Medical Records (EMR), telemedicine, and Enterprise Architecture (EA). This study uses a qualitative analysis method supported by literature studies and case studies in Indonesia. The main challenges identified include system interoperability issues, data security and privacy, implementation costs, and resistance to change. To address these challenges, the study proposes using strategic gap analysis to assess integration gaps and identify areas for improvement. In addition, implementing EA with the TOGAF framework is expected to improve the coordination and integration of health information systems. Data standardization through implementing FHIR is also essential to strengthen system interoperability. This study recommends developing policies that support the adoption of health technology and the exploration of new technologies in diagnosis. Through this approach, the study aims to improve the efficiency, quality, and overall accessibility of primary healthcare services.

articleTitle: Social Commerce Sentiment Analysis on YouTube Comments with Lexicon-Based and Long Short-Term Memory Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Recently, social media platforms have included buying and selling features. Some social media platforms have added certain features to facilitate the buying and selling process, hence the term social commerce. TikTok Shop is the most popular social commerce platform user in Indonesia. The phenomenon of TikTok Shop's rapid social commerce growth coincides with the issue of predatory pricing practices that impact the decline in local MSME turnover. There is a lot of discussion about this issue on the YouTube video platform, but the sentiment orientation is not yet clear. This study aims to explore public sentiment related to issues that arise on TikTok Shop using a lexicon-based approach and a deep learning algorithm, namely Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). 5 popular YouTube video channels that discuss TikTok Shop obtained a total of 14,644 comments. The comment from 14,045 data after passing the text preprocessing stage is labeled with the results of 9,576 data grouped into negative sentiment comments, 2,620 positive comments, and 1,849 neutral comments. The analysis results show that public sentiment on TikTok Shop tends to be negative with most comments expressing concern about the issue of predatory pricing practices that harm MSMEs. This research proves that LSTM is able to classify public sentiment on YouTube comments discussing TikTok Shop based on the results of testing the best hyperparameter combination with the number of neurons as many as 64 units and dropout 0.4 obtained an accuracy value of 92.34%.

articleTitle: Optimizing Feature Extraction for Website Visuals: A Comparative Study of AlexNet and Inception V3
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This study investigates the feature extraction capabilities of two prominent convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, Inception V3 and AlexNet, in the context of website visuals. With the growing need for automated visual data analysis on the web, effective feature extraction is critical for tasks such as image classification, object detection, and visual content analysis. Inception V3 and AlexNet were selected due to their distinct architectural approaches and widespread use in various computer vision applications. The research employed a controlled experimental design, utilizing a dataset of website visuals collected from platforms like Themeforest. Data preprocessing included image resizing, normalization, and augmentation techniques to enhance model robustness. Both models were fine-tuned on the specific dataset to adapt their pretrained weights from ImageNet to the unique characteristics of website visuals. Performance metrics were used to evaluate the models' effectiveness, including precision, recall, F1 score, Mean Average Precision (MAP), and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG). Results indicated that AlexNet outperformed Inception V3 in precision (0.7062 vs. 0.6860) and recall (0.5914 vs. 0.0506), highlighting its efficiency and suitability for more straightforward feature extraction tasks with lower computational costs. In contrast, Inception V3 exhibited superior potential in capturing complex visual patterns but struggled with computational efficiency, as evidenced by its significantly longer inference time (222.9552 seconds compared to 63.2978 seconds for AlexNet). The findings underscore the importance of model selection based on specific application requirements, such as prioritizing speed or depth of feature extraction. Recommendations for practitioners include leveraging AlexNet for resource-constrained environments and opting for Inception V3 when handling complex, multi-scale visual data. Future research could explore additional architectures and optimize models to enhance performance across diverse visual tasks.

articleTitle: Level of Readiness and User Acceptance of E-Recruitment Applications: Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This study explores the readiness and acceptability of e-recruitment applications in an era of rapidly developing mobile technology, where they reflect the shift from conventional to digital methods of job searching. This research method involves examining accredited journals related to readiness to implement e-recruitment applications, with a focus on journals that have been published and that can combine personality and technology dimensions. This research focuses on best practices and challenges in application development, where the level of user readiness and acceptance of e-recruitment applications can be measured from the user and technology sides. The combination of these two points of view highlights the importance of applications in understanding the factors that influence technology readiness and acceptance, so that they can optimally meet user expectations.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Urban Heat Island Prediction in Malang City Using Remote Sensing Data
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This study investigates the Urban Heat Island (UBI) phenomenon in Malang City, Indonesia, utilizing advanced remote sensing technologies and machine learning methods to enhance Land Surface Temperature (LST) predictions. Urbanization, driven by infrastructure development outlined in Regional Regulation No.4 of 2011, has led to a significant reduction in green open spaces, exacerbating the UBI effect. We leverage Google Earth Engine (GEE) to integrate satellite data from Landsat-8 and Sentinel-2, alongside elevation data from the Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM). Employing various predictive models, including Support Vector Regression (SVR), Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost, this research introduces the Urban Density Index (UDI) and elevation as critical variables impacting UBI dynamics. The study employs Z-score normalization to standardize data ranges, significantly improving model accuracy. Results indicate that SVR outperforms other models with the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.662 and a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.854. Strong correlations are observed between UDI (0.91) and LST, highlighting urban density as a key contributor to elevated temperatures, while elevation shows a negative correlation (-0.41), indicating cooler conditions at higher altitudes. These findings underscore the importance of integrating UDI and elevation in UBI analyses, contributing valuable insights for urban planning and environmental management in rapidly urbanizing areas.

articleTitle: Social Media Marketing and Electronic Word of Mouth on Customer Preference and Choice in Over-the-Top Media Service Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The increase in the number of top media service platforms in Indonesia is an interesting phenomenon to be studied. The large selection of top media service platforms requires companies to compete for consumers. The choice of the right marketing tools in attracting consumers to choose the top media service platform is social media marketing and electronic word of mouth. In digital marketing strategy, electronic word of mouth is one of the considerations of consumers in choosing the products they will consume. This study employed a quantitative research methodology. Basic research, or pure research, is included in this study. The study will be conducted among Netflix subscribers. A questionnaire and a review of the literature were used as data gathering methods in this investigation. Respondents to the study were given a questionnaire with five Likert scales as the research tool. The research concludes that Social Media Marketing does not significantly influence Customer Preference or Customer Choice, while E-WOM (Electronic Word of Mouth) has a substantial impact on both.

articleTitle: Optimizing Field Technician Collaboration Through Implementing Digital Twin Technology in IT Service Management
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The automotive world nowadays has experienced significant and rapid growth. These changes are focused on how conventional cars transform and expand using IoT, combined digital collaboration. The complexity around IT service management in automotive manufacturers also needed solutions to enhance collaboration among field technicians to improve service delivery. This article proposes a conceptual framework for optimizing field technician collaboration by implementing digital twin technology within IT Service Management. Digital twin technology, which entails the development of virtual representations of tangible assets and systems, presents significant opportunities for improving decision-making, communication, and operational efficiency. By integrating digital twin technology with established IT Service Management practices, this framework aims to streamline the coordination and performance of field technicians, thereby elevating overall service quality. The framework outlines key stages such as data collection, model creation, simulation, analysis, and optimization.

articleTitle: Mobile Islamic Banking Consumer Behaviour in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The challenge of managing digital banks is in managing technology and convincing consumers to use it. The purpose of this study is to analyze the intention and behavior of using Islamic mobile banking by adopting the UTAUT 2 variables. Data were collected by distributing online questionnaires using Google Form. The data collected from 117 respondents were then analyzed using the Structural Equation Model Partial Least Square (SEM - PLS) technique using SmartPLS Software version 3.3.0. The results of the study show that social influence, experience and habits have a significant influence on the intention to use Islamic mobile banking. Performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and price values have a positive relationship, but their influence is insignificant. While facilitating conditions and hedonic motivation have a negative relationship, their influence is insignificant. The intention to use mobile banking has a significant effect on the behavior of using Islamic mobile banking. Facilitating conditions have a positive relationship but the effect is not significant. Islamic banks need to focus on setting strategies to increase social influence and user experience to encourage customer intentions to use Islamic mobile banking, which will ultimately affect Islamic mobile banking behavior.

articleTitle: Switching Behavior Analysis of E-Government Application Using the Extended UTAUT Model
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: To improve population administration services, the government has developed an e-government initiative in the form of a Digital Population Identity (IKD) application. IKD is a solution to the process of making a physical E-KTP (Electronic Population Card) which takes quite a long time. Although the government has set a target of 25% of E-KTP holders activating IKD in 2023, the realization is only around 3.3% who have activated it. Based on these conditions, it is necessary to examine the factors that influence IKD application users to switch from E-KTP to the IKD application using the Extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) model. The population of this study was IKD application users in Java, with a total of 406 respondents selected through a proportional stratified random samplingtechnique. Data analysis was carried out using the PLS-SEM approach with SmartPLS version 4.1. The results of the study showed six variables that significantly influenced user behaviorto switch from E-KTP to IKD. Namely the variables of performance expectations, social influence, perceived risk, perceived security and privacy, trust, and intention to switch. In contrast, expectations of effort, supportive conditions, and government support did not have a significant effect. The variables of perceived security and privacy showed the highest significance, with a t-test value of 54.339 and a p-value of 0.000,while the variable of government support showed the smallest impact, with a t-test value of 0.354 and a p-value of 0.723. These findings can provide direction for Dukcapil to improve the implementation and increase public acceptance of the IKD application.

articleTitle: The Effect of E-Leadership and Innovative Work Behavior on Employee Performance: The Mediating Role of Technology Adoption
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The flow of change in information technology is developing very quickly. These changes have a significant impact on employee work behaviour in the organization. Human resources must increase their competence and adapt to technological advances. Technology adaptation must be done so the organization is not destroyed by technology itself. The Surabaya City Population and Civil Registration Service implements Electronic Government. The implementation of e-government was realized by creating the Klampid New Generation application, which aims to make it easier for the public to manage the registration of marriages, births, deaths, movements and arrivals. The implementation of the technology application process is greatly influenced by the e-leadership leadership style, namely, someone who carries out their leadership functions through technology. Leaders and employees are also required to adapt to technological advances because the rapidly changing work environment and intense competition increasingly place demands on how employees work. Technology adoption will influence employees' ability to generate new ideas, encouraging innovative work behaviour and improving organizational performance. This research analyzes the influence of e-leadership and innovative work behaviour on employee performance through adaptive technology as mediating variables. A total of 200 employees tasked with providing Population and Civil Registration data for the City of Surabaya were respondents. This research is explanatory, and The data collected was processed using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) analysis technique. This research hypothesizes that e-leadership and innovative work behaviour significantly influence the application of technology. E-leadership and innovative work behaviour influence employee performance. This research also emphasizes that adopting technology influences employee performance and mediates the relationship between e-leadership, innovative work behaviour, and employee performance.

articleTitle: Exploring the Relationships between Dynamic Capabilities, Digital Transformation, and IT-Business Alignment
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Business and IT alignment is crucial to business organizations, navigating digital transformation, leveraging dynamic capabilities, facilitating smooth integration of digital technologies, and creating competitive added value in managing digital. Nevertheless, there is no literature discussing the influence of dynamic capabilities in doing business and IT alignment through digital transformation in managing digital business. The objective of the research is to explore and ensure the full impact of the digital transformation construction in bringing business and IT alignment together with every indicator of the effects of dynamic capacity with the availability and readiness to manage a digital business-convergence triangulation research method with explanatory design through follow-up explanation. The research population was taken from all the digital businesses that had run them for at least five years. 198 of the 238 respondents completed the questionnaire online through Google Forms using a random sampling technique with a response rate of 83.19%. The Likert scale is used to process and analyze data using the SEM-PLS method. The results of the research showed it turns out that the assumption of managing digital business is very resistant to the need to harmonize business and IT from the influence of digital transformation is not proven at all, and the existence of the linkage of dynamic capabilities in carrying out the alignment of business and IT.

articleTitle: How Social Engineering Information-Seeking Intention Mediating Information-Sharing Intention in Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) has become an essential component of modern life in the digital era. However, it also presents vulnerabilities that can be exploited for cybercrimes, such as social engineering attacks that are prevalent on social media platforms. The imperative to seek information about social engineering and disseminate it to others is critical for enhancing information security awareness among social media users. This study aims to identify the factors that influence the intention to share information and examine how the intention to seek information mediates these factors in relation to the intention to share information. This research integrates the Theory of Planned Behavior and the Protection Motivation Theory frameworks to provide a comprehensive understanding of the determinants of information-seeking behavior related to social engineering on social media. The variables under investigation include attitude, subjective norm, perceived threat, information-seeking intention, and information-sharing behavior. A quantitative research methodology is employed, utilizing PLS-SEM analysis with a sample size of 200 participants. The findings indicate that attitude, subjective norm, and perceived threat significantly impact the information-seeking intention regarding social engineering on social media. Notably, only the subjective norm directly influences the intention to share information. Nevertheless, the intention to seek information has a direct effect on the intention to share information and also mediates the influence of other variables. Theoretical and practical implications are discussed concerning strategies for enhancing information-sharing behavior among social media users.

articleTitle: Implementation of Web-Based Metaverse Virtual Classes Integration in Academic Education
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Integrating web-based virtual classes in university settings within the metaverse represents a transformative approach to education, offering immersive and interactive learning experiences. This research aims to explore the practical application of this innovative method in Indonesian education while identifying any discrepancies with existing theories. By employing usability testing, the study seeks to provide an analysis of the implementation of web-based virtual classes in university. Usability testing in this context can help identify usability issues and improve the overall user experience of the learning system. Using usability testing to provide valuable insights from users, including students and educators, regarding the functionality and user-friendliness of the virtual learning environment. The primary objective of this research is to bridge the gap between theoretical frameworks and practical implementation of web-based virtual classes in Indonesian university using usability testing based on Jakob Nielsen's theory which has never been used in this case in the previous studies. Previous studies found that the application of metaverse is effective in education, but others explain practically still have any lacks. By examining the actual application of this technology, researchers could maximize the aim to enhance teaching and learning practices. From this research, we found out that, web-based virtual classes are usable for learning activities and could help pave the way for more tailored and effective educational strategies in the metaverse. Through this study, we found what aspects we need to consider to develop a web-based metaverse virtual class.

articleTitle: Technology Readiness Measurement in Middle-Level School Learning for Business Process Reengineering to Support Digital Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Implementing Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in education is inevitable. However, since the implementation of ICT is not cheap and could take many resources, many aspects must be considered. Much research shows that top management support and good information technology (IT) design are important factors in the six steps of IT implementation to support digital learning in reengineering business processes. But almost none or few take the digital readiness of the educational workforce relation for the successful IT implementation in education into account. So this paper finds out how the digital readiness on education relates to IT transformation to support Digital Learning and what instrument should be prepared and revised to support it.

articleTitle: Analysis of Spelling Errors in Text Data Using Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Spell checking is a step in correcting errors in a text. This research uses the Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) model to carry out machine learning-based spelling error analysis. In this research, we explored the dataset and corpus used with the aim of making it easier for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) models to analyze spelling errors. This research uses data originating from social media and web-based text communication platforms with a total of 1000 data. The Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) model can read complex spelling error patterns based on training data and also pay attention to linguistic context and pay attention to syntax in the text so that this model can produce better spelling corrections with an accuracy rate of up to 94%. In this model there is a first, second and third test, each of which yields an accuracy. The first test produces 87% accuracy, the second test produces 90% accuracy and the third test produces 94% accuracy. After that, an evaluation was carried out using ROC (Receiver Operating Characteristic) which produced a value of 0.94. The use of machine learning in this model can help in data analysis so that data patterns are detected properly, so that spelling errors can be corrected. This research has shortcomings in terms of the complexity of the very long time in the training process due to the large amount of data and corpus used to produce good accuracy.

articleTitle: Design and Development of History Learning Media Prototype to Enhance Student Engagement and Comprehension: Integration of SDLC and Bloom's Taxonomy
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This study develops interactive learning media centered on Indonesian female heroes, utilizing SDLC and Bloom's Taxonomy up to the Applying (C3) level. The prototype includes biographies, multiple-choice questions, and interactive puzzles to boost student engagement and comprehension. Results show 87% of students experienced increased engagement, 80% improved their understanding, and 83% provided positive feedback on the user experience. The prototype effectively guides students from Remembering and Understanding to Applying knowledge interactively. While successful, feedback suggests refining the puzzle difficulty to better match students' abilities. This study demonstrates how integrating Bloom's Taxonomy into interactive tools can deepen historical understanding and promote gender equity in education. The prototype has practical implications for classroom use, supporting gradual learning progression. Future research will focus on adjusting the challenge levels for broader learner suitability.

articleTitle: Indonesian Abstractive Text Summarization with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM)
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Every language is unique, including Indonesian text. In the development of text summarization, research is mostly oriented to extractive methods, which have an unreadable sentence structure. The abstractive summarization has a more natural summary, but the process is more challenging than the extractive method. Therefore, this research aims to produce an Indonesian abstractive text summary using Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM), which can produce abstractive summarization for English texts well. So, in this study, Bidirectional LSTM is used to improve the quality of the Indonesian text summary. Also, local attention is added to assist the model in predicting the summary. The results of evaluating the model on the Indonesian language article text show that the model can capture the essence of the summary text. The ROUGE evaluation shows that Bi-LSTM with local attention can produce an Indonesian abstractive summary well.

articleTitle: Efficiency Analysis of Commercial Banks in the Era Digitalization Financial Sector: A Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The rapid development of technology in Indonesia has an impact on various sectors, one of which is the financial sector. Digitalisation of the financial sector is unavoidable and a necessity. The covid-19 pandemic has also forced conventional people to switch to using technology. One of the financial sector digitalisation products is digital payment systems such as link aja, Gopay, Ovo and so on. The challenge of banking digitalization is getting stronger with the existence of various factors that encourage the development of digital banks in Indonesia, considering that Indonesia has great economic potential to absorb digitalization development. The contributing factors are represented in three main aspects: digital opportunities, digital behavior and digital transactions. There are at least two most significant potential positive impacts that may arise from digital transformation by banks. First, expanding the accessibility of banking, second, increasing the competitiveness of Indonesian banking. Digital banking will be able to increase the ease of access to banking for the public, as well as increase banking efficiency so that it will encourage increased economic activity. The purpose of this study was to determine the level of efficiency of Indonesian and Malaysian banks. In this study the data used is secondary data sourced from the publication reports of Indonesian and Malaysian banks in 2019–2022 Meanwhile, the research method used is DEA (Data Envelopment Analysis) The results of the study explain that there are 3 Indonesian banks that are consistently efficient and there is 1 bank that is only efficient in 2022. While Malaysian banks there are only 2 that are consistently efficient and 2 more are not efficient. When viewed from the average efficiency, Indonesian banks are more efficient faster but if there is a shock that comes from external (covid-19) then Indonesian banks will immediately decrease their efficiency. In contrast to Malaysian banks that tend not to experience shocks during the covid-19 pandemic, they actually crawl up even though they are not 100% efficient.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis and Topics Modeling on Mobile Banking Reviews of Sharia Bank in Indonesia Using Naive Bayes and Latent Dirichlet Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: BSI Mobile and Muamalat DIN are mobile banking apps from two Shariah banks in Indonesia, available on the Google Play Store. User reviews on these platforms feature varied writing styles, making sentiment modeling with Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and classification with Naive Bayes challenging. This study addresses these challenges by employing LDA for sentiment topic modeling and enhancing classification with Naive Bayes. Data was collected through web scraping, resulting in 45,000 reviews for BSI Mobile and 6,515 for Muamalat DIN. After labeling, the BSI Mobile dataset included 25,940 positive and 9,695 negative sentiments, while Muamalat DIN had 826 positive and 424 negative sentiments. LDA identified four key topics for each app, with coherence scores of 0.424 (BSI Mobile) and 0.337 (Muamalat DIN). Sentiment classification achieved 81.60% accuracy (AUC 0.89) for BSI Mobile and 78.40% accuracy (AUC 0.85) for Muamalat DIN, using an 80:20 data split. This research presents a novel, integrated model for more accurate LDA-based sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: User Acceptance Analysis of Investment Applications Among Millennials and Generation Z Using the Extended UTAUT 2 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Investment applications are digital platforms that enable users to engage in various investment activities, such as buying and selling stocks or other investment instruments, through internet-connected devices. Despite the convenience and accessibility offered by investment applications, the interest in investing among Millennials and Generation Z remains low, at 4.21% and 7.41% of the total population of these generations, respectively. This issue underscores the importance of research to understand investment preferences and the factors influencing the acceptance of investment applications among these generations. This study employs the UTAUT 2 model with the addition of trust and perceived security variables to evaluate the acceptance of investment applications. A quantitative approach was adopted, distributing an online questionnaire comprising 35 questions. The study population includes users of investment applications from Millennials and Generation Z, with a sample of 389 respondents obtained through purposive sampling. The data analysis method used is PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4.0. The results show that out of 12 hypotheses tested, 8 were accepted. Variables influencing behavioral intention include habit, social influence, effort expectancy, price value, and trust. Variables affecting use behavior include behavioral intention, habit, and facilitating conditions. The 4 rejected hypotheses are performance expectancy on behavioral intention, facilitating conditions on behavioral intention, hedonic motivation on behavioral intention, and perceived security on behavioral intention. This study provides insights into investment preferences and the factors influencing the acceptance of investment applications among these generations. It is useful for investment application developers to enhance user acceptance, particularly among Millennials and Generation Z.

articleTitle: Tracing the Development Methodologies of Software Engineering: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: A systematic literature review using the PRISMA framework identified the most widely used software engineering development methodology in scientific research and its distribution in various research fields in the last decade (2015–2024). This research aims to analyze the use of software development methods. Using the Publish or Perish and Mendeley tools, the identification of several papers shows that the Agile methodology, especially Scrum, still dominates current software development practices because of its flexibility. There is a trend of combining Agile with approaches such as APLE and SME. The methodology has also spread to the educational field with BYOS to teach software engineering concepts and human-computer interaction with Agile to teach computational thinking. Formal methods are used to guarantee product quality. These findings provide a comprehensive overview of the current state and trends in software development methodology adoption across various research domains.

articleTitle: Utilizing Sentiment Analysis to Enhance Customer Feedback Systems in Banking
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The banking industry faces challenges in effectively capturing and analyzing customer feedback, particularly in identifying the true sentiments and opinions of customers. Conventional feedback systems often lack accuracy and are slow to respond to customer needs and complaints, which can negatively impact customer satisfaction and loyalty. To address this issue, this study aims to enhance customer feedback systems by utilizing sentiment analysis, a natural language processing (NLP) technique capable of categorizing customer opinions as positive, negative, or neutral. The research method involves collecting customer feedback data from various sources such as social media, surveys, and online reviews. This data is then analyzed using sentiment analysis algorithms designed to identify emotional patterns in the text. The results indicate that the use of sentiment analysis significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of customer feedback processing, enabling banks to provide faster and more relevant responses to customer needs. In conclusion, sentiment analysis can significantly strengthen customer feedback systems in the banking sector, offering banks better insights into customer sentiments in real-time. This ultimately contributes to improved customer satisfaction and loyalty, as well as enhancing the quality of services provided.

articleTitle: Efficient Student Academic Support: Leveraging Indonesian BERT for Question Answering in Chat Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This study focuses on the application and accuracy measurement of the Indonesian Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (IndoBERT) model within the context of a student academic service chat feature. The primary data utilized in this research is derived from interviews conducted with academic service staff who assist students majoring in informatics engineering. This real-world data provides the context needed for the model to function effectively in understanding and responding to student inquiries. To further enhance the model's comprehension of the Indonesian language, secondary data from the Wikipedia dataset is also employed, serving as a supplementary knowledge base. The research methodology adheres to the Indonesian National Work Competency Standards (SKKNI) No. 299 of 2020, specifically within the Artificial Intelligence and Data Science Sub-Sector. The practical deployment of the model is carried out through the integration of a chatbot on the Telegram application, providing a user-friendly interface for students to interact with the system. The accuracy of the IndoBERT model is evaluated using a confusion matrix, a standard tool in machine learning for assessing classification accuracy. The results are promising, with the model achieving an impressive accuracy score of 96.6%. This indicates that the IndoBERT model is highly effective in question-answering scenarios, particularly in supporting the Indonesian language.

articleTitle: Evaluating Usability of a Digital Learning Website Using ISO/IEC 9126–4
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Agensip Creative Agency is one of the creative industry start-ups that has launched the Agensip Class website. Agensip Class is a digital learning website for young people who are interested in learning about the creative sector. In the use of a website, user satisfaction is a factor that affects the effectiveness and efficiency when the website is used. This study aims to determine the usability level of the Agency Class website in terms of effectiveness, efficiency, and user satisfaction. In addition, this study was conducted using a Usability testing approach with 30 respondents and by using the Labyrinth Design tool. Based on the results of the evaluation that has been carried out, it can be seen that the calculation of the effectiveness of the website is in accordance with ISO/IEC 9126–4 which produces a value of 69.9%. Meanwhile, the final result of the degree of efficiency based on time-based efficiency calculations is 0.0171366833 a second. In addition, the findings of usability testing with the Maze Design tool resulted in a usability score of 64. Furthermore, for the grade scale this website is in grade C, namely good with a score of 75.6 which indicates that users are quite satisfied in using the website.

articleTitle: Assessing Technology-Driven Financial Inclusion Strategies in Emerging Markets: An Empirical Study
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Economic progress depends on financial inclusion, especially in emerging nations where a sizable segment of the population lacks access to banking. This research aims to evaluate the efficacy of technology-driven financial inclusion initiatives in Indonesia, focusing on the influence of perceived utility, perceived simplicity of use, and technological trust on the uptake of these services. A quantitative approach was employed using a survey of 263 respondents, with SmartPLS utilized to analyze the data for assessing construct validity and reliability and examining proposed correlations. The findings reveal that trust in technology emerged as a significant barrier, negatively impacting user adoption, while perceived usefulness and convenience of use positively influence adoption. However, there is a discrepancy between the potential benefits of these technologies and their actual adoption, as indicated by the non-significant association between financial inclusion outcomes and technology adoption. The novelty of this study lies in highlighting the critical need to address trust issues and improve user experience to enhance the use of digital financial services in emerging nations. Actionable insights derived from these findings can aid policymakers and financial service providers in better promoting financial inclusion through technology.

articleTitle: The use of Software Testing Techniques in Software Development: Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: In the modern digital era, software has become the backbone of various aspects of life, which makes software testing an essential step in development to detect and correct defects, thereby producing quality products according to user needs. The purpose of writing this Systematic Literature Review (SLR) is to see various types of utilization of testing software in development software. The method used in this study is literature review with utilizing typeset tools, Mendeley and Google Translate to support the research process. The results of this research provide an overview of various software testing techniques that can be used in various software development contexts, as well as the importance of conducting appropriate testing to ensure the quality and reliability of the final product.

articleTitle: Fuzzy-Set Qualitative Comparative Insights: Understanding Student Intentions in Digital Crowdfunding Investment
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Crowdfunding investing has emerged as a compelling alternative for the general population due to its ability to provide easier and quicker access to a wide range of financial instruments, thereby altering the conventional approach to investing. The literature concentrates on utilizing the theory of planned behavior, configured with convenience, to forecast the intention to invest in crowdfunding. The study conducted a fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis of 136 Indonesian tertiary students who participated in crowdfunding through digital platforms. Our aim was to discover and examine the configuration determinants that affect high and low students' investment intentions. The findings indicate that in order to promote a high intention to invest in crowdfunding through a digital platform, it is crucial to align attitudes and subjective norms with convenience. Conversely, a lack of alignment between subjective norms and perceived behavioral control leads to a lower crowdfunding investment intention through a digital platform. Moreover, this research offers useful perspectives for digital crowdfunding platforms to enhance the promotion of crowdfunding services in Indonesia. This aids the digital crowdfunding platform in comprehending investor preferences in order to stimulate investment intentions. Eventually, this study has added to the expanding body of empirical research on investment intentions in crowdfunding through digital platforms and has shown the efficacy of the proposed theoretical framework in identifying possible explanations for the low investment intentions through digital platforms among university students.

articleTitle: Gamification Analysis and Design on Arabic Learning for Indonesian Elementary School Student
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: An Integrated Islamic Elementary School is a school that combines general and religious (Islamic) education into one curriculum. An Integrated Islamic Elementary School is a school that combines general education and religious education into one curriculum. Arabic is one of the subjects that students must study. Conventional learning methods can make students feel bored and fed up. Gamification is an effective approach to attract students' interest in learning. Gamification involves using game design elements and techniques in nongame contexts. The interactive design created using figma, and deployed using React Framework. Design evaluation used A/B testing in maze.com, System Usability Scale (SUS) to evaluate the high fidelity prototype and web application also. The results of the SUS score of 78,33 for the prototype, and 78,44 for the web apps. Its indicate the design acceptable for the user and good to deploy. The User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) identified innovation and creativity aspects of the design need to be improved.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Strategic Management: A Bibliometric Study of Emerging Trends and Future Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This study explores the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into strategic management from 2015 to 2024, examining AI's impact on decision-making, operational optimizaTion, and competitive advantage. A bibliometric analysis was conducted on 5,668 articles to visualize key trends, contributors, and research themes. The United Kingdom, United States, and China significantly contribute to this field. Prominent authors such as Kumar and Chatterjee are driving recent trends, while Parida and Dwivedi have provided foundational insights. The study underscores the importance of leading journals in shaping the research landscape and highlights the need for international collaboration, ethical considerations, and the development of advanced analytical tools. Recommendations include leveraging big data, enhancing predictive capabilities, exploring practical applications, and fostering human-AI collaboration to advance strategic management.

articleTitle: Behavioral Intention to Use Telemedicine Applications Among Millennial and Generation Z in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Telemedicine applications such as Halodoc, Alodokter, and KlikDokter serve medical consultation and treatment which are vital aspects of human life. However, in practice there are still users who experience problems in using the application. Based on reviews on the Google Play Store related to the telemedicine application, there are users who complain about the length of response time, application performance that does not match expectations, discrepancies in services with the price paid, misunderstanding of information between patients and doctors, bugs in features, and even difficulty in accessing the telemedicine application. These problems are indicated to affect User Satisfaction and Behavioral Intention of users in using telemedicine applications. Generation X - those born between 1960 and 1980 are the most satisfied with telemedicine, whereas Millennials and Generation Z are more fluent in the use of technology. This study uses a quantitative approach with a population of telemedicine application users among Generation Z and Millennials in the Greater Jakarta Area. Sampling with purposive sampling involved 500 respondents who met the criteria. Data analysis using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS version 4. The Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT 2) integration model with the Delone & McLean model is used to determine the factors that influence Behavioral Intention of telemedicine application users. The results of the study indicate that of the 8 hypotheses, there are hypotheses Effort Expectancy on User Satisfaction and Social Influence on User Satisfaction that are rejected. Behavioral Intention variable is most influenced by User Satisfaction. This research provides an understanding of the factors that influence the behavioral intentions of telemedicine application users based on the perspective of each user of the application. This can be useful for telemedicine application providers as a consideration for increasing user satisfaction, especially in maintaining user behavioral intentions to use the application.

articleTitle: Evaluation of User Experience in the Lecture Activity Menu of AIS Mobile for Student Using Heuristic Evaluation, System Usability Scale and User Experience Questionnaire
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Syarif Hidayatullah State Islamic University is a public university in Jakarta. This university is very much following the times by launching a Learning Management System commonly called AIS Mobile. There are several opinions from users of this application that the user interface and appearance of this application are less friendly. As a result, many designs of this application do not keep up with the development of existing application designs and the author also has suggestions regarding features that are useful for users in the future and for application developers. Data collection begins with observation, followed by literature study and interviews. In the design stage, the User Centered Design (UCD) method is used, consisting of four steps, namely context of use analysis, user needs analysis, solution design creation, and solution design evaluation. The results of evaluating the solution design using the Heuristic Evaluation (HE) method, System Usability Scale (SUS), and User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) show that the solution design created has been assessed quite well and users can interact effectively and easily. Comparison of the evaluation results between the initial AIS Mobile for Students lecture activity menu and the evaluation results using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) method shows a significant improvement, with an average difference in improvement of 1.12. The Heuristic Evaluation (HE) method shows that the solution design has 4 problems that fall into the low priority category. While in the SUS method, the average usability score of the solution design is 80 with an acceptance level that falls into the acceptable category. In conclusion, the solution design has successfully overcome the problems that existed in the initial design by providing convenience for users in accessing information more quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Adaboost Regressor in Diamond Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Besides being in great demand in the form of jewelry, diamonds are one of the hardest materials ever on earth. Some communities are starting to look at diamonds to become investment assets, considering their extraordinarily high value. However, problems are found when diamonds do not have a reference price like other investment assets such as gold or stocks. Therefore, in line with technological developments, this research aims to implement machine learning algorithms in diamond price forecasting. The methods used in this research are the Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbors, and Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost) Regressor algorithms, which were chosen to be compared. The dataset used in this study comes from Vittoriogiatti's Kaggle repository, with a total of 53,940 lines. The results of this study indicate that the Random Forest Regressor comes out as the best algorithm among the other two, with an average error value of 19.85 (MSE train), 132.73 (MSE test), 4.45 (RMSE train), 11.52 (RMSE test) and the average training duration is 13.73 seconds. The R2-Score value is 0.981, and predictions are produced with a very small difference from the original value of 0.2. The KNN Regressor algorithm has an average R2-Score value of 0.964. While AdaBoost Regressor with an average R2-Score of 0.884.

articleTitle: Learning Management of Islamic Religious Education Based on Digital Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The research in this study posits that the management of Islamic Religious Education (PAI) learning, when integrated with digital technology, must align with Islamic values; religious education should not rely solely on digital technology, as teachers play a vital role in serving as role models. This study aims to analyze the management practices for integrating digital technology into PAI instruction. The findings reveal that character-based PAI learning incorporating digital technology meets four critical elements: (1) digital teaching modules and a Learning Management System (LMS), (2) digital technology-based learning infrastructure, (3) teacher training, and (4) mentoring to guide student character development. This research employs a qualitative, descriptive-analytical method with a phenomenological approach, focusing on lived experiences of teachers and students within the PAI context. Data collection methods include in-depth interviews with educators, observations of classroom practices, and document analysis of digital learning materials and LMS usage. The collected data are then coded and thematically analyzed to identify patterns in the adaptation of digital tools while maintaining core Islamic educational values. Primary data were collected directly from the Islamic Development Network (IDN) in Bogor, providing a practical case for examining digital integration in PAI.

Author Keywords: Islamic Religious Education (Pendidikan Agama Islam/ PAI)

articleTitle: A Bibliometric Analysis: Challenges and Opportunities of Implementing Time Management Technology for Flexible Work in the Service Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The service sector has witnessed a surge in flexible work arrangements, prompting the exploration of time management technology's impact on efficiency and adaptable work environments. This research employs a bibliometric analysis with a qualitative approach through literature review. Data will be sourced from the Scopus database and analyzed using bibliometric mapping and content analysis to gain a comprehensive understanding of how time management technology influences time flexibility in the service sector. This study aims to identify emerging opportunities and challenges, focusing on the gap between existing research and the specific needs of IT-enabled business process reengineering (BPR). The analysis will explore how technology can optimize flexible work practices without compromising employee well-being and organizational integrity. By integrating insights from bibliometric analysis and recommendations for optimal technology use, this study will contribute valuable knowledge for organizations seeking to leverage technology for improved time management in a flexible work environment.

articleTitle: Unlocking Regulatory Technology on Fintech Use Among Indonesian Students: A Triad of Financial Literacy, Inclusion, and Risk Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Global finance has been substantially affected by the rapid proliferation of financial technology (fintech), and Indonesia is currently no exception. Interest in fintech solutions among students is increasing as a result of the Indonesian government's ongoing efforts to improve financial literacy. This research employs quantitative data collection and analysis. We conducted a comprehensive survey of 450 respondents from a variety of Indonesian university. Route analysis in this investigation is preferred to be conducted using SmartPLS 3.0. In this investigation, the potential of regulatory technology (RegTech) to mitigate the impact of students' financial literacy, financial inclusion, and risk tolerance on their utilisation of fintech is investigated. The findings of this study suggest that regulatory technology is a critical component that can serve as a source of positive reinforcement for individuals who possess financial literacy, financial inclusion, and risk tolerance, thereby enabling them to utilise fintech effectively and responsibly. Regulatory technology can moderate financial inclusion on fintech use. This information can assist policymakers, educational institutions, and fintech companies in the development of regulations that are focused and that integrate regulatory technology to provide students with a more comprehensive and secure financial environment.

articleTitle: The Role of RegTech in Automating Compliance and Risk Management
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The growing complexity of regulatory requirements in the financial services industry has intensified the need for efficient compliance and risk management systems. Regulatory Technology (RegTech) offers a solution by automating compliance processes. This study evaluates the effectiveness of RegTech in automating compliance and risk management tasks and identifies the challenges involved. The research is guided by the question: How effective is RegTech in enhancing compliance efficiency while mitigating operational risks? A mixed-methods approach was used, with data collected from 205 financial institutions, including banks, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies that have adopted RegTech. The findings show significant improvements in compliance speed and accuracy, though challenges persist with legacy system integration and the need for skilled personnel. The study emphasizes RegTech's role in reducing operational risks and promoting sustainable financial practices, aligning with Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure). The results suggest that institutions implementing RegTech will see enhanced compliance efficiency, reduced risks, and improved sustainability. This research pro- vides valuable insights for financial institutions aiming to leverage technology for optimizing compliance strategies and gaining a competitive edge.

articleTitle: Opportunities and Challenges of Distributed Ledger Technology in Cross-Border Financial Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This research investigates the adoption of Dis- tributed Ledger Technology (DLT) in cross-border financial transactions, driven by the increasing need for more efficient, secure, and transparent methods in a globalized financial market. Traditional cross-border transactions often face challenges such as delays, high costs, and security risks, making DLT a promising solution with its ability to provide secure, immutable, and trans- parent transaction records. The study focuses on understanding how trust, security, perceived usefulness, and perceived ease of use influence the adoption of DLT. Conducted with 150 respondents, primarily young adults from Jakarta and Tangerang, the research employed Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM–PLS) to test six hypotheses. The results of this study indicate that both Trust and Security have a positive and significant impact on the adoption of Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) in cross-border financial transactions. Utilizing the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS- SEM) method, addressing the growing need for more efficient, secure, and transparent methods in global finance. These findings hold significant practical implications for financial institutions, suggesting that enhancing trust and security in Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) systems can lead to broader adoption and ultimately improve the efficiency and transparency of cross- border financial transactions. These findings underscore the critical importance of trust and security in promoting DLT adoption in cross-border transactions, suggesting that efforts to enhance these factors will be crucial for broader acceptance of DLT. Future research should explore additional variables, such as regulatory frameworks and cultural factors, that may also affect DLT adoption in different regions.

articleTitle: Decoding Arabica Coffee Purchase Intention: Exploring the Role of Product Origin Through Fuzzy-Set Qualitative Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The purchase of arabica coffee has become a prominent preference among consumers owing to its exceptional characteristics and unique provenance, which have impacted the conventional method of coffee ingestion. The existing body of literature centers on the application of the TPB, with the addition of the notion of product origin, in order to predict the propensity to purchase arabica coffee. A fsQCA was performed on a sample of 246 Indonesian consumers of arabica coffee who indicated an intention to purchase. The objective of this study was to identify and analyze the configuration determinants that influence consumers' intentions to stimulate high or low purchases. To increase the likelihood that an individual will purchase arabica coffee, it is essential to align attitudes with the perceived value of the product's origin, according to the findings. On the contrary, participation in matters pertaining to product origin, attitude, and subjective norms does not result in an increased inclination to buy Arabica coffee. Furthermore, this study provides valuable insights for managers in the coffee industry regarding how to improve the marketing of arabica coffee through emphasizing its place of origin. This facilitates the comprehension of consumer preferences by coffee producers, thereby encouraging intentions to make purchases. This study has ultimately contributed to the growing corpus of empirical research concerning purchase intentions in relation to the origin of the product. Furthermore, it has demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed theoretical framework in discerning potential rationales for both elevated and diminished purchase intentions of arabica coffee.

articleTitle: ICT Implementations: Typology of Using Digital Platforms for Efficient Business Performance in Microfinance Institutions a Bibliometrix Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The most complete application of ICT is currently only in microfinance on a large scale, including internet banking and mobile banking, cloud computing, big data analysis and blockchain. Meanwhile, in microfinance institutions, the digital platforms used are limited to mobile phones with internet-based online platforms to simplify operational performance. This research aims first to map research on ICT implementation around the world published in reputable international journals and indexed by Scopus. Second, analyzing the network of variable relationships in ICT implementation. Third, to analyze digital platform use in microfinance institutions (MFIs). The results of this study in the last 21 years from 2003–2024 only found 83 articles on ICT implementation in microfinance. Then there are 4 research clusters related to ICT implementation in microfinance. Furthermore, the digital platforms most widely used by microfinance are internet banking and mobile banking at 79.92%. While big data analysis, cloud computing and block chain are still far below 20%. This research is an initial step in mapping several variables and indicators for further development, especially ICT implementation in Indonesia, which is still very rarely done.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Impact of AI-Mediated Interactions on Student Outcomes in Online Learning: A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: The educational landscape is rapidly evolving, with a growing emphasis on integrating technology into the learning process. However, the effectiveness of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) in enhancing student performance remains a topic of debate. This study delves deeper by specifically examining the influence of interactions between instructors and students mediated by Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems on student performance and anxiety within online learning environments. Utilizing bibliometric analysis techniques, this research offers a systematic analysis of existing literature to identify trends, gaps, and patterns in the research surrounding technology-driven education. By focusing on specific disciplines like mathematics and literacy, the study aims to reveal potential variations in the impact of technology based on subject matter and educational level. This analysis is expected to provide novel insights to guide the design and implementation of educational technology that fosters effective and inclusive learning. Additionally, the research intends to offer practical recommendations for optimal technology integration in various educational contexts (data analysis, business processes, etc.). Ultimately, this study aspires to contribute to improved educational quality through the strategic and impactful utilization of technology.

articleTitle: Transforming Modern Marketing: Artificial Intelligence Implementation for SEO Marketing of Online Store in E-Commerce Marketplace
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in e-commerce apps allows businesses to personalize the shopping experience for their customers. AI can recommend relevant products, create personalized product descriptions, and generate realistic product images by analyzing customer data and shopping patterns. With the help of AI, e-commerce apps can provide targeted recommendations based on customers' preferences and browsing history. This research focuses on a case study of AI implementation in Natural Language Generation (NLG), Image Generation, Chatbots and Virtual Assistants, Recommendation Systems, and Price Optimization as part of SEO Marketing in e-commerce apps. With a case study research approach in one of the global e-commerce marketplace apps, it is hoped that this research can provide thorough research on AI in e-commerce apps and valuable insights into its potential applications and implications for achieving digital marketing goals for e-commerce apps.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Necessity for Assistance in Utilizing E-Filing for Individual Tax Reporting
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This study explores questions surrounding the capacity of taxpayers to file their personal tax reporting electronically, offering the case of UIN Syarif Hidayatullah Jakarta to assess the effect of technological advancement on actual compliance of members of the academic profession. The quantitative method employed correlational techniques in investigating the interaction between ease of use, the length of time taken to file taxes electronically, and assistance needed by various users during the process of e-filing. As per the study conducted in 2022, there seems to be no significant relationship between ease of use and assistance need (Pearson correlation = - 0.021, p-value = 0.847) and a very weak relation between time experience and assistance need (Pearson correlation = 0.079, p-value = 0.473). The overall premise is that while e-filing technology has been developed as a means of making tax processes easier, tax is processes have not been fully eliminated. This research also analyzes the reporting procedure of personal taxes with regard to e-filing tax system and identifies the factors responsible for peoples' subjective views towards the system such as the ease of use, general online experience and the level of digital insecurity. Understanding of taxpayer behavior helps to determine what aspects of user training, service, and system usage should be improved to increase compliance. The tax assistance program still retains its relevance, as does its internal management.

articleTitle: Modeling Madd Reading Classification in Surah Al-Fatihah with MFCC Feature Extraction and LSTM Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: Currently there is no standardization that regulates the length and shortness of madd readings. This research aims to classify madd recitation in Surah Al-Fatihah using Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficient (MFCC) feature extraction and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithm. This research uses the Machine Learning Life Cycle method and begins with the Data Collection process in the form of recording to capture qira'ah data, then audio conversion is carried out and the results will be cut to select the madd section. MFCC feature extraction is used on the selected audio and the results are used to train the classification model using the LSTM algorithm. After that, the model was tested using Confusion Matrix, from two types of models and three scenarios of data separation ratio tested, the best performance was achieved in model b scenario 2 using a data separation ratio of 80:20 and 4 LSTM layers with 64 units. The dataset used amounted to 100 data, with 80 data for training and 20 data for testing. The model achieved training accuracy of 96.88% and testing accuracy of 90.0%. The results of this study provide information and knowledge about madd tajweed classification to readers, that madd tajweed classification has never been done in previous studies and show that the LSTM algorithm and MFCC feature extraction are suitable for use in this classification model.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Feature Selection Methods in Classification of Thyroid and Heart Disease Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: High-dimensional data cause serious problems in the scalability and performance of machine learning algorithms. Feature selection is a preprocessing method that selects important features from high-dimensional data sets to improve the efficiency and accuracy of pattern recognition. This study uses two public datasets, namely Differentiated Thyroid Cancer Recurrence (dataset1) and Heart Disease Classification (dataset2). The stages of this research are preprocessing, feature selection, classification, and performance evaluation. The experiments used three feature selection methods, namely ReliefF, Lasso, and Random Forest. As for the classification using SGDClassifier. The results show that Random Forest consistently shows good performance, achieving high ROC area scores (0.99 for thyroid disease and 0.82 for Heart Disease) and effective classification error reduction. ReliefF also showed good performance, while Lasso had a less stable and lower performance than other methods. Unfiltered features generally show strong initial performance but are less stable than feature-selected models. Overall, in this study Random Forest was used as a feature selection method with stable performance due to its balanced performance in both datasets.

articleTitle: Conceptual Model of Loyalty on Mobile AIS Users Using the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM)
publicationTitle: 2024 12th International Conference on Cyber and IT Service Management (CITSM)
abstract: This study aims to propose a conceptual model for measuring the loyalty of Academic Information Systems (AIS) mobile application users at Universitas Islam Negeri (UIN) Syarif Hidayatullah Jakarta. The proposed model was derived from the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM) by incorporating four essential variables in ECM: confirmation, perceived usefulness, satisfaction, and IS continuance intention. The initial model added five supporting variables: information quality, system quality, trust, habit, and loyalty. The nine variables were combined in one conceptual model and then used as a proposed research model. Finally, this study has ten hypotheses about evaluating AIS mobile application services on user loyalty. The results of this study are in the form of a conceptual model to be used to measure the loyalty of AIS mobile application users in the selected universities in Indonesia. Based on reviewing past studies related to the topic, this conceptual model enriches the variety of loyalty by adopting several variables in previous research models, which are then added to the Expectation Confirmation Model (ECM) as the basic model.
